chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

When the boy reaches his full strength at thirteen years and enters his fourteenth year, whatever is obligatory upon those who have reached puberty becomes obligatory upon him, whether he experiences a wet dream or not. His evil deeds are recorded against him, and his good deeds are recorded for him. Everything becomes valid for him except if he is weak-minded or foolish.

key_terms.أَشُدَّهُ: his full strength or maturity in the context of age-based legal responsibility
key_terms.سَفِيهًا: foolish or feeble-minded, lacking sound judgment
key_terms.ضَعِيفًا: weak, meaning lacking adequate mental or practical capacity
key_terms.ٱلسَّيِّئَاتُ: evil deeds recorded against a morally accountable person
key_terms.ٱلْحَسَنَاتُ: good deeds recorded in a person's favor
key_terms.ٱلْغُلَامُ: the boy; the male child under discussion
key_terms.ٱلْمُحْتَلِمِينَ: those who have reached puberty, literally those experiencing puberty signs

ai.seo_question: When do religious obligations and legal responsibility begin for a boy in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a boy, upon reaching thirteen years and entering his fourteenth year, becomes subject to the obligations and moral accountability of those who have attained puberty, even if no wet dream has occurred. It also indicates that full legal capacity is recognized for him unless he is mentally weak or foolish.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5519 - Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa' narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdullah (as), who said: "

When a boy reaches the age of thirteen and enters into his fourteenth year, what is obligatory upon those who have reached puberty becomes obligatory upon him, whether he experiences a wet dream or not. His bad deeds are recorded against him, and his good deeds are recorded for him. Everything becomes permissible for him except if he is weak-minded or foolish."
